verses.text: Article the First: every crew shall sail one ship, and the ship shall have a trunk that holds the canon. A crew divided among two hulls is two crews, and two crews sharing one flag is a mutiny waiting for weather.

Article the Second: the name upon the stern is the ship and not the cargo. Azazael is neither product, nor promise, nor client; paint the name true, for a false flag invites the wrong enemies and the wrong friends.
Article the Third: no gun shall be called loaded until it has been fired. An unexercised control is a decoration, and decorations do not sink ships nor save them; fire the gun, then speak of it.
Article the Fourth: articles are not enforced by being written, but by the captain's hand. A rule that nothing runs is a shanty, and shanties, though fine for rowing, have never stopped a leak.

Article the Fifth: another ship's charts are counsel and not course. Verify them against thine own soundings, in these waters, before trusting the hull to them; many a good ship lies on reefs marked safe by others.

paragraphs: Every pirate ship sails under articles, signed by the whole crew, stating shares, discipline, and the law of the deck. Bartholomew Roberts carried eleven; this book carries fifteen, restating the corpus in articles no sailor can misread. Sign them or sail elsewhere.

verses.text: Every number shall be written with the command that produced it. Shares are divided by the count, and the count by the articles; a share claimed without the reckoning behind it is theft with better manners.
A count is true of the tree it was taken from; quoted a week later it is a memory wearing a number's clothes. Count the shares at division, not at dreaming; rum promised is not rum poured.
How long shall a row be called closed, when the verb that closed it was not a verb the queue knew? The purser who marks debts paid with an ink the ledger never heard of will swing, or wish he had.

She never lays a finding at a door without first running the control that proves whose door it is. Blame, like treasure, must be dug where it lies; accuse the wrong door and the crew will remember whose word dug there.
The interpreter was measured live, and the measure was written down. Weigh the gold in sight of the crew, with scales all can see; secret measures breed mutiny faster than short rum.

paragraphs: Quarrels over shares sank more crews than storms. This book restates the corpus law of honest reckoning — cited numbers, witnessed counts, proven doors — in the idiom of men who divide treasure and know exactly what a false count costs.

verses.text: A probe reported an accelerator that was not in this box, because the reading came from another venv. Many ships have steered by another vessel's lights and woken on another vessel's rocks; keep thine own lookout, whatever the fleet signals.
The dead store is not a metaphor. It is a row nobody reads, counted twice and reported as coverage. Barnacles on the hull, counted as crew: scrape them, for they eat and do not row.
A mirror is not a corpus; a copy answers for the day it was taken. An old chart is a memory of water, not water; sail by it and the reef will teach thee the difference, gratis.

A character is measured where its assets live; a render that has never been read is a plan with a file name. A ship counted by its figurehead is a figurehead with a crew attached; reckon the hull, not the carving.

A tree that is not in the repository is not missing; it is elsewhere. Land ho cried at an empty horizon is a mistake; land ho cried at the wrong island is a wreck. Mind the difference before concluding.

paragraphs: Old sailors mark wrecks on their charts that the young may sail around them. This book marks the corpus wrecks — false lights, dead stores, old charts, figureheads, empty horizons — in the voice of men who survived them and came home to warn the harbor.

edition.basis: a themed edition of The Book of the Tree in the voice of the pirate articles: law of the deck, honest reckoning, and marked wrecks, with a citation on every verse back to the verse it restates
edition.name: The Annotated Pirate Code
